title: The Resurrection of the Righteous and the Unrighteous
speaker: Pastor Steve Brinegar

outline.title: Resurrection as a Foundational Biblical Truth
subpoints: Early expression in the Old Testament (Job)
Paul's testimony in Philippians and 1 Corinthians
Jesus' declaration in John 11 and Matthew 22

outline.title: The Nature and Types of Resurrection
subpoints: Distinction between resurrection of life and judgment

outline.title: The Two Phases of the Final Resurrection
subpoints: Resurrection at the beginning of the millennium
Resurrection at the end of the millennium
Consistency of this theme throughout Scripture

summary:
This lecture, the fourth and final installment of the 2020 Ron Tabor Lecture Series, addresses the doctrine of the resurrection, specifically distinguishing between the resurrection of the righteous and the unrighteous. The speaker emphasizes that while eschatological views may vary, the reality of bodily resurrection is a foundational truth of biblical Christianity, affirmed by both the Old and New Testaments. The teaching highlights that the resurrection is not merely a future event but a present hope that motivates Christian service and sanctification, as seen in the writings of Paul and the teachings of Jesus.

The lecture outlines that the final resurrection occurs in two distinct phases: the first resurrection of the righteous at the beginning of the millennium and the second resurrection of the unrighteous at the end. This distinction is presented as a consistent theme throughout Scripture, rather than an isolated concept found only in Revelation 20. The speaker encourages believers to approach these texts with grace toward those holding different eschatological systems, while firmly grounding their understanding in the authority of God's Word.

Ultimately, the resurrection is portrayed as the cornerstone of the Christian faith, linking the creation narrative in Genesis to the consummation in Revelation. It serves as the ultimate hope for believers, transforming their lowly bodies to be like the glorious body of Christ, and stands as a testament to God's power to conquer death and sin.
